h1: The 8 Best NETGEAR Network Switches for Home and Small Office, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best NETGEAR Network Switches: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 NETGEAR network switches scored on port count, PoE budget, managed features, fanless design and mounting options.
summary: The NETGEAR GS308EP is the switch to buy if you run PoE cameras or access points and want per-port control. The GS305P is the cheaper PoE route for four devices, the GS308E is the best managed switch for VLANs on a budget, and the GS308 and GS316v3 are the dependable unmanaged choices when you only need more ports.
intro: Buyers usually pick a switch by port count and regret it later, because the label that matters is not the number of jacks but what each jack can do. A plain unmanaged switch moves traffic and nothing else. A PoE model also powers cameras and access points, and a smart managed model lets you separate traffic into VLANs. Choosing the wrong class costs far more than choosing the wrong port count.

This ranking groups eight NETGEAR switches by capability first and size second. We reviewed the spec sheets and listings, focusing on port count, PoE budget, management features, cooling and mounting. We do not quote throughput numbers beyond what is listed, and we flag where a listing leaves a detail open.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308EP 8-Port PoE+ Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: Eight PoE+ ports with per-port control, and PoE that keeps running during a reboot.
products.description:
The GS308EP is an 8-port Easy Smart managed switch with PoE+ on every port at roughly 62W total. It offers per-port PoE control and keeps PoE uninterrupted during a reboot, so cameras do not drop out when the switch restarts. Pricing lands between $50 and $100.

It takes the top spot because it combines the two features home labs and small offices want most: power over Ethernet and basic management. Per-port control lets you power-cycle a frozen camera or access point from the web interface instead of walking to it. The budget is shared across all eight ports, so a few hungry devices can use it up quickly. Check each device's wattage against the roughly 62W total.

Buy it if you power cameras, phones or access points over the cable and want some control. Skip it if nothing you own needs PoE.
pros: Per-port PoE control from the web UI
products.idealFor: Small offices powering cameras and access points.
products.skipIf: None of your devices use PoE.

products.name: NETGEAR GS305P 5-Port PoE Gigabit Switch
products.verdict: Four PoE+ ports sharing 63W with dynamic power reallocation, fanless and unmanaged.
products.description:
The GS305P has five ports, four of them PoE+, with a total budget of 63W and dynamic power reallocation. It is fanless and unmanaged, and sits in the $25 to $50 bucket.

It takes the runner-up spot because it covers a common need cheaply: powering a couple of cameras or an access point without an extra injector. Dynamic reallocation shifts spare watts to the port that needs them, which stretches the budget. Without management you cannot reboot a single port remotely or split traffic into VLANs, which is why the GS308EP outranks it.

Choose it for a small setup with up to four powered devices. Skip it if you want remote port control or more than four PoE ports.
products.idealFor: Two to four PoE devices on a small network.
products.skipIf: You want to manage ports or VLANs.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308E 8-Port Easy Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: Up to 64 VLANs, a cross-platform web GUI and automatic DoS, loop and storm protection.
products.description:
The GS308E is an 8-port Easy Smart managed switch supporting up to 64 VLANs, with a cross-platform web interface and automatic protection against DoS, loops and broadcast storms. It sits under $25.

It ranks third because it delivers managed features at the price of a basic switch. A VLAN lets you keep smart home gadgets, guests or a work laptop on separate networks, which is the real reason to buy a smart switch. It has no PoE, so it cannot power devices. The web GUI is simple but not a replacement for a full managed switch, and you need a router that understands VLANs to benefit.

Buy it if you want to learn VLANs or segment traffic cheaply. Skip it if you need PoE or just want to plug devices in.
pros: Web GUI works on any platform
products.idealFor: Home networkers who want VLANs on a budget.
products.skipIf: You only need extra ports, or need PoE.

products.name: NETGEAR GS308 8-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Eight gigabit ports in a fanless metal housing, with energy-efficient Ethernet.
products.description:
The GS308 is a plain 8-port gigabit unmanaged switch in a fanless metal housing, with 802.3az energy-efficient Ethernet and desktop or wall mounting. It sits under $25.

Fourth place reflects a straightforward role. It adds ports and nothing else, which is exactly what many desks and TV stands need. The metal case helps shed heat without a fan, so it makes no noise. Compared with the GS308E it lacks VLANs and monitoring, but it is simpler and avoids any configuration at all.

Buy it if you need to expand a router that is short on ports. Skip it if you want management or PoE.
pros: Eight gigabit ports at a low price
products.idealFor: Adding ports to a desk or media cabinet.
products.skipIf: You want VLANs or powered ports.

products.name: NETGEAR GS316v3 16-Port Fanless Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Sixteen fanless gigabit ports for a larger home or workshop.
products.description:
The GS316v3 provides 16 gigabit ports, fanless, with 802.3az energy-efficient Ethernet and desktop or wall mounting. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Sixteen ports are overkill for most homes, but ideal for a house with wired rooms, a home lab or a workshop. Being fanless is a real advantage when the switch sits in a living space. It is unmanaged, so all ports share one flat network. Check the amount of cabling you will run, because a full switch behind a TV unit becomes a tangle.

Buy it if you wire many rooms or devices. Skip it if eight ports cover you.
products.idealFor: Houses with many wired rooms or devices.
products.skipIf: Eight ports are plenty for you.

products.name: NETGEAR GS324 24-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: Twenty-four fanless ports that mount on a desk, wall or rack.
products.description:
The GS324 offers 24 gigabit ports, fanless, with auto-negotiation and energy-efficient Ethernet, and can mount on a desk, wall or rack. It sits in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Sixth place reflects how few buyers need it. For a small office or a home network rack, twenty-four ports is a convenient single box that avoids chaining switches. The rack option stands out against the smaller models. It remains unmanaged, with no PoE, so a larger office would want a managed or PoE switch instead.

Buy it if you are cabling a rack or a full office floor. Skip it for ordinary home use.
cons: Far more than a home needs
products.idealFor: Small offices and rack-based home labs.
products.skipIf: A typical home network is all you run.

products.name: NETGEAR GS305E 5-Port Easy Smart Managed Switch
products.verdict: A five-port smart switch with VLAN, QoS and port monitoring in a fanless case.
products.description:
The GS305E is a 5-port Easy Smart managed switch offering VLAN, QoS and port monitoring, fanless and energy-efficient. It sits under $25.

It ranks seventh because five ports leave little room for growth, and the GS308E gives you eight ports plus more VLAN headroom for a similar price. The QoS option can prioritize traffic such as video calls, and port monitoring helps with troubleshooting. It suits a desk where one or two segments are enough.

Buy it if you want smart features on a tiny footprint. Skip it if you expect to add more devices soon.
pros: VLAN and QoS in a tiny switch
cons: Only five ports to grow into
products.idealFor: A compact desk setup needing basic management.
products.skipIf: You may outgrow five ports quickly.

products.name: NETGEAR GS305 5-Port Gigabit Unmanaged Switch
products.verdict: The cheapest way to turn one Ethernet jack into five, fanless and energy-efficient.
products.description:
The GS305 is a 5-port gigabit unmanaged switch, fanless, with 802.3az energy-efficient Ethernet and desktop or wall mounting. It sits under $25.

It lands last only because it does the least. If your router has one free port and you need a few more for a TV, console and PC, it solves the problem with no setup at all. It lacks the management of the GS305E and the power delivery of the GS305P, so check what your devices need before choosing the cheapest.

Buy it if you simply need more ports. Skip it if you need PoE or VLANs.
products.idealFor: Adding a few wired devices to a router.
products.skipIf: You want any smart or powered features.

whatMatters.detail: An unmanaged switch needs no setup and treats every port the same. A smart managed switch adds a web interface for VLANs, QoS and monitoring. Pick managed only if you will use those features, since they add complexity. Look for the words Easy Smart managed on the listing.

Power over Ethernet sends power and data on one cable, but the switch has a total wattage shared across ports. A 63W or 62W budget can run a few cameras but not many high-draw devices. Add up your devices' wattage and compare it with the switch total before buying.

Five and eight ports suit a desk or TV cabinet, while sixteen and twenty-four ports suit wired houses and offices. Leave spare ports for growth. Count current wired devices, add a few, and remember that one port is used by the uplink to your router.

Fanless switches make no noise and have no fan to fail, which matters in a bedroom or living room. They rely on a metal case to shed heat. Check the listing for fanless, and give the switch some airflow instead of burying it.

Desktop, wall and rack mounting decide where the switch can live. A rack ear kit matters in a network cabinet, while wall mounting keeps cables tidy at home. Check the listing for the mounting options, and confirm the screws or brackets are included.

faq.q: Do I need a managed switch at home?
faq.a: Most homes do not. A managed switch matters when you want VLANs to separate smart home gadgets, guests or a work network. If you only need more ports, an unmanaged switch is simpler and cheaper.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake when buying a switch?
faq.a: Counting ports but ignoring PoE. If your cameras or access points need power over Ethernet, a plain switch leaves you buying injectors. Check the wattage budget too, since it is shared across ports.

faq.q: Is the GS308EP worth over the GS305P?
faq.a: It is if you want per-port control, eight powered ports and uninterrupted PoE during reboots. The GS305P is enough for up to four devices without management. Choose by how many powered devices you have.

faq.q: How do I set up an Easy Smart switch?
faq.a: Connect it to your network, find its address through the maker's discovery tool, and open the web interface. Set a password first. Make VLAN changes carefully, because a wrong setting can cut off your own connection.
They are designed to shed heat through the case, so they run fine with some airflow. Avoid stacking items on top of them or burying them in a closed cabinet. Wall mounting gives good airflow.

faq.q: Will a gigabit switch slow my internet?
faq.a: A gigabit switch will not slow a typical home internet plan below gigabit speeds. The bottleneck is usually the connection from your provider or Wi-Fi. A faster switch only helps for multi-gigabit links.

finalTake: The NETGEAR GS308EP is the best overall switch, combining PoE+ on eight ports with per-port control. The GS305P is the budget way to power a few cameras, and the GS308E is the smartest low-cost managed switch. If you only need ports, the GS308 and GS316v3 are the simple, silent picks.
